title: Rum and Raisin Ice Cream
subtitle: Old-school custard ice cream with dark-rum-soaked raisins
excerpt: A vanilla custard ice cream with dark-rum-soaked raisins folded in during the last minute of churning. Soak the raisins overnight, or longer, for the best result.
sourceNotes: Rum and raisin ice cream has been a fixture of British seaside and parlour ice cream since at least the 1950s. The combination of dark rum and dried fruit has deep roots in British cooking, particularly in the baking tradition of rum-soaked fruit for Christmas puddings and cakes. The ice cream version translates those flavours into a frozen custard.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. The rum in the raisins keeps them slightly soft even when frozen.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Soak the raisins in rum overnight or up to a week ahead. The custard base can be made the day before churning.

content.text: Rum and raisin is a custard ice cream with dark-rum-soaked raisins folded in during the last minute of churning, the alcohol in the raisins keeps them pliable and slightly soft in the finished frozen scoop, and the rum bleeds gently into the custard during soaking. The custard itself is plain vanilla; the rum and raisin combination carries the whole flavour. Soak the raisins at least overnight and up to a week for maximum depth.

items.prepNote: for soaking the raisins, use a good quality dark rum

content.text: Place 120g raisins in a small bowl and pour over the dark rum. Stir to combine, cover, and leave to soak at room temperature for at least 8 hours, ideally overnight. The raisins will plump up and absorb most of the rum. Drain before adding to the ice cream machine, reserving any remaining rum to stir into the custard base for extra flavour.

Whisk the egg yolks and caster sugar together in a large heatproof bowl until pale and thickened. Combine the milk and cream in a medium saucepan and heat to just below boiling. Pour the hot cream mixture slowly onto the yolks, whisking constantly, then return to the saucepan over a low heat. Stir continuously for 8 to 10 minutes until the custard thickens and coats the back of the spoon. Remove from the heat, stir in the vanilla extract and any reserved rum from the raisin soak. Pour into a clean bowl, press cling film onto the surface, and cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

Churn the cold custard in an ice cream maker for about 25 minutes until thick and softly set. In the last minute of churning, add the drained rum raisins through the lid of the machine. Transfer to a freezer-safe container, seal, and freeze for at least 6 hours or overnight.

items.symptom: Raisins are hard in the finished ice cream
items.cause: The soaking time was too short, or very dried-out raisins were used.
items.fix: Soak for at least 24 hours. Plump, fresh-looking raisins will soften more readily. A brief warming in the rum over low heat (not boiling) for 2 minutes before the overnight soak can help very dried raisins.

items.symptom: Raisins sank to the bottom of the container
items.cause: They were added too early in the churning process before the ice cream was thick enough to suspend them.
items.fix: Add the raisins in the very last minute of churning when the machine is working against a thick, stiff mixture. Transfer to the container quickly and freeze without stirring.

items.cause: Freezing suppresses alcohol flavour, and the rum may have been absorbed entirely into the raisins.
items.fix: Reserve 2 tablespoons of rum from the soak and stir directly into the cooled custard before churning. This keeps a rum note in the base itself, not just in the raisins.

content.text: Keeps in the freezer for up to 3 months. The alcohol in the raisins means they stay slightly soft even from fully frozen, they will not be hard. Allow 5 minutes before scooping.
